extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors and contributors writing or editing mathematics articles for a general audience
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing, formatting, and structuring mathematics content on Wikipedia so it is accessible to general readers while remaining precise for specialists. Covers article structure, prose style, notation, typesetting, proofs, algorithms, and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead section accessibility and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead section must be accessible to a general reader. State alternate names in bold. Provide informal motivation, history, and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the lead comprehensible to non-specialists; include bolded alternate names and informal material (motivation, history, applications) rather than technical definitions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article body ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Body introduces formal definitions in dedicated 'Definition' sections, then theorems, then examples, then proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this ordering to keep exposition clear: definitions first (in a dedicated section), followed by theorems, illustrative examples, and proofs placed afterwards so readers encounter concepts before technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: End sections placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalizations, 'See also', 'References' sections at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve higher-level or ancillary material and bibliographic items for the article's end to avoid interrupting the main exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a picture before mathematics when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture before mathematics whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an illustrative image or diagram early to provide intuition for general readers before presenting formal mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't begin a sentence with a symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't begin a sentence with a symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start sentences with words; if a symbol must appear, rephrase so prose leads and symbols follow (e.g., 'Let n be...' rather than starting with 'n is...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid textbook-style rhetorical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid textbook-style rhetorical devices ('Note that', 'Obviously', 'It is easily seen that', leading questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use phrases that presume reader insight; prefer neutral phrasing explaining why a statement holds to avoid alienating or confusing readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize the authorial 'we'
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the authorial 'we'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use impartial, encyclopedic voice; avoid conversational collective pronouns unless they improve clarity without introducing informality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blackboard abbreviations in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid blackboard abbreviations: no 'wrt', 'wlog', 'iff' in prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write out phrases in full in running text (e.g., 'without loss of generality', 'if and only if', 'with respect to') to be clear to wider audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace symbols with words in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace symbols with words in prose: write 'for all' rather than ∀, 'in' rather than ∈.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use words for logical/connective symbols in running English sentences so prose reads naturally to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the ambiguous 'any'
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the ambiguous 'any'; use 'every' or 'some'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Any' can be ambiguous between universal and existential quantification; choose 'every' (universal) or 'some' (existential) for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use 'if and only if' in definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use 'if and only if' in definitions; rephrase as 'is defined to be'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In definitions state membership or identity positively (e.g., 'X is defined to be ...') rather than using biconditional phrasing which can be stylistically awkward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define every variable before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Define every variable before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce symbols and variables with a clear definition the first time they appear in the article or section to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain formulas with words
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain formulas with words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany mathematical expressions with explanatory prose describing the meaning of terms and the intuition behind the formula; avoid leaving formulas unmotivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rings conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings are assumed associative and unital; non-unital rings are 'rngs'. Exception: operator algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly when deviating from these assumptions (e.g., when discussing non-unital examples or operator algebras).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Compact spaces are not assumed Hausdorff (state Hausdorff explicitly when needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state 'compact Hausdorff' when both properties are required; don't silently assume Hausdorff from 'compact'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural numbers convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural numbers: be explicit whether 0 is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the convention used in the article (N = {0,1,2,...} vs N = {1,2,...}) to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subset symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets: use ⊆ for subset, ⊊ or ⊄? (page says) use ⊂= (text: 'subset' = \subseteq) for subset, \subsetneq for proper subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise with subset notation: use \subseteq for subset and \subsetneq for proper subset to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix transpose notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrix transpose: superscript non-italic T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typeset the transpose as a roman (upright) superscript T rather than an italic variable to distinguish it from other superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed formulae typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Displayed formulae: prefer LaTeX (`<math display=block>`).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LaTeX display math for multi-line or important equations for consistency and readability; prefer <math display=block> markup on Wikipedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline formulae consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline formulae: no consensus; HTML or LaTeX, but never mix in one expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mix HTML and LaTeX within a single inline mathematical expression; pick one markup style consistently within an expression or article where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italicize variables, not numerals or function names
rubrics_metrics.description: Italicize variables, never numerals or function names like sin, log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set variables in math italics; keep numerals and standard function names upright to conform with mathematical typesetting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Greek letters upright
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital Greek: not italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not italicize capital Greek letters; reserve italics for variables only where conventional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function names in upright font
rubrics_metrics.description: Function names: use upright font (sin, cos, log).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typeset standard function names in roman (upright) font so they are distinguished from variables (e.g., sin(x) not sin⁡(x) in italics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sets of numbers formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets of numbers: bold ℝ or LaTeX \mathbb{R} — be consistent within an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \mathbb or bold styling consistently for common number sets (ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, ℝ, ℂ) throughout the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication in formulae: juxtaposition; in explanations for general readers, use ×.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In symbolic formulae omit explicit multiplication signs (use ab), but in explanatory prose or for clarity to general readers use the × symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minus sign character
rubrics_metrics.description: Minus sign: U+2212 −, not hyphen-minus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the proper Unicode minus character (U+2212) in rendered math rather than the ASCII hyphen-minus to ensure correct spacing and appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscripts/superscripts HTML markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscripts/superscripts: HTML <sub>/<sup>, not Unicode characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using special Unicode subscript/superscript glyphs; use proper HTML or math markup tags for subscripts and superscripts for accessibility and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman numerals ASCII-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Roman numerals: ASCII letters only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typeset Roman numerals using ASCII characters (I, V, X, etc.) rather than special glyphs to avoid encoding issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain formulas in prose rather than bullets
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain via prose, not bullet lists, when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer natural-language explanations of formulas and symbols; use bullets only when they genuinely improve readability for lists of items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label and describe variables in prose examples
rubrics_metrics.description: 'where b is the … vector, a is the … coefficient, and r is the … vector'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting an equation, name and briefly describe each symbol in the surrounding sentence to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation after formulas must follow English rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation after a formula must be the natural English punctuation (period, comma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat formulas as part of the sentence: include the appropriate punctuation mark immediately following the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place punctuation inside inline math tags
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX in inline use, place punctuation inside the </math> tag to avoid line-wrap orphans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write <math>...formula...</math>,. with the comma/period inside the math element so line breaks do not leave punctuation stranded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include proofs only when illuminating
rubrics_metrics.description: Include proofs when they illuminate concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display proofs that provide insight, intuition, or indispensable understanding; avoid including routine or technical proofs that do not aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude purely correctness-only proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude proofs that only establish correctness without insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit long technical proofs that only verify results unless they are historically or pedagogically important; consider linking to sources instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set proofs apart for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Set apart proofs in collapsible boxes or separate sections so the article remains readable to those who don't want to read them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collapsible elements, dedicated 'Proof' subsections, or separate pages to prevent proofs from interrupting the main exposition for casual readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms: prefer pseudocode
rubrics_metrics.description: Pseudocode preferred over a specific language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present algorithms in clear, language-agnostic pseudocode to be accessible to readers from different programming backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms: use syntax highlighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use syntax highlighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including code or pseudocode blocks, use markup that provides syntax highlighting to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms: include one implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: One implementation; not many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single representative implementation rather than multiple versions in different languages; link to external repositories when multiple implementations are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite historical papers for important theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite historical papers for important theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide primary-source citations for theorems' origins and significant developments to support verifiability and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer linking to free online sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Link to free online sources where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor open-access versions of papers or reliable free resources so readers can verify claims without paywalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability is mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifiability is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All factual claims, theorems, and historical attributions must be verifiable via reliable sources; unsourced assertions may be challenged or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ≡ vs = in definitions — use = unless modular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer '=' for definitions and equalities unless you mean a congruence or modular equivalence where '≡' is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set difference notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \setminus for set difference, never `\` alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid plain backslash notation; use the standard \setminus operator to denote set difference to prevent ambiguity and rendering issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ∘ for composition (LaTeX `\circ`), not Unicode ring operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typeset function composition with the LaTeX \circ symbol to ensure correct spacing and appearance rather than arbitrary Unicode characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner product notation
rubrics_metrics.description: `\cdot` for inner product (or use ⟨·,·⟩), never juxtaposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make inner products explicit with \cdot or angle-bracket notation rather than leaving ambiguity via simple juxtaposition, or clearly define the convention used.
